newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Mark/yen dip girds dollar/mark for battle.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Mark/yen dip girds dollar/mark for battle.

text.p: Weakness in the mark/yen cross has temporarily capped dollar/yen, but provided dollar/mark with a springboard for retesting its recent three-year highs, technical analysts said.
On Monday dollar/mark peaked at 1.7375, its highest level since the week ending February 27, 1994, before tumbling back towards support in the 1.7270 area on Tuesday.
But key support near 1.7225 has not been seriously threatened, suggesting dollar/mark could resume its rally in the near future, said John Tirone, technical analysts at Chase Securities Inc.
"We really pulled back from that high, but the only way we get a test of the downside is if we get below 1.7220 (marks) today. I like the way the market is holding here," Tirone said.
Chartists said a seven-day support line in the 1.7225 marks area gives the dollar a solid short-term foundation.
"While we're above that level, we have the potential to see further upside gains. You've got to stay with this trend," said Scott Siller, technical analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch.
Siller added that a break of 1.7230 would signal corrective weakness in dollar/mark.
Mark/yen's continuing stay below 73 bolsters dollar/mark and keeps dollar/yen under downward pressure, though support seems to be holding near 125.50 yen, chartists noted.
"The real catalyst is mark/yen, which has entered a corrective phase," said Siller.
Mark/yen appears relatively stable near 72.75, but downside objectives sit just lower at 72.50 and 72 the figure. Those levels represent Fibonacci retracements, Siller noted.
With mark/yen waning, dollar/yen could slip toward supports resting at 124.80 and 124.25, technicians said.
"Daily studies show some bearish signals," Siller said.
But should dollar/yen hold above 125 or so, fresh tests of its 57-month high near 127.20 could ensue in coming sessions, some chartists said.
"We're really starting to enter a wide congestion area and we've got to start closing above 126.75-80 (to test the highs)," said Tirone. "I would continue to buy dips here."
Elsewhere, sterling continued its widely expected retreat from its 55-month high near 2.8250, but held its ground near 2.7950 and bounced above 2.80 after a bout of profit-taking.
